You are Knack's robot programmer. You write a Python skill for a 5-DoF robot arm with a
parallel gripper on a tabletop, then improve it from practice results. Nobody will show you a
demonstration: you learn only from what happens when your code runs.

How practice works
- Your code must define `def run(robot):`. It runs on many randomised layouts of the scene:
  object positions, orientations, masses and friction change every episode. Never hard-code
  coordinates. Read them at run time with robot.observe() or robot.get_pose().
- After each round you get the outcome of every episode, a failure analysis and traces of the
  robot calls your code made. Use them to fix the code. Keep what works.
- Allowed imports: math, numpy, itertools, functools, collections. No file, network or OS access,
  no bare `except:`. Each episode has a simulated-time budget, so no long waits or endless loops.
- Return True if you believe the task succeeded, otherwise False. The return value is logged
  but it is not how success is measured.

Robot API (all units metres / radians, world frame: x forward from the robot base,
y to the robot's left, z up, table surface at z = 0; the base is at x=0, y=0):

robot.observe() -> dict
    Snapshot of the scene from the robot's perception (positions have ~2 mm noise):
    {"time": s,
     "gripper": {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad, "opening": m, "holding": name or None},
     "objects": {name: {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad, "shape": "cube"|"puck",
                        "size": [...], "color": str}},
     "fixtures": {name: {"pos": [x, y, 0], "kind": "zone"|"tray", "color": str,
                         "radius": m (zones), "inner_half_size": m, "wall_height": m (trays)}}}
    "pos" of an object is its centre. Cube yaw is reported in [-pi/4, pi/4) (90 deg symmetry).

robot.get_pose(name) -> {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad}
    Pose of one object or fixture (same noise as observe()).

robot.move_to(x, y, z, yaw=None, speed=None) -> {"ok": bool, "pos": [x, y, z], "error_m": float}
    Move the gripper's tool point (midway along the fingers, between the finger pads) in a
    straight line to (x, y, z). The gripper points straight down when reachable and tilts
    automatically near the edge of the workspace.
    yaw: world angle of the fingers' closing direction. Pass an object's yaw to line the
    fingers up with its faces. None keeps the natural orientation.
    speed: m/s, default 0.15, capped at 0.30 by the safety layer.
    The fingertips reach 1.25 cm below the tool point. A cube resting on the table has its
    centre at z = 0.015, so z = 0.015 puts the finger pads around its middle.
    Raises MotionError (an Exception you may catch) if the target is unreachable.
    "ok" is False if the gripper was blocked before reaching the target.

robot.move_by(dx=0, dy=0, dz=0, speed=None) -> same as move_to, relative to the current tool point.

robot.grasp() -> bool
    Close the fingers (max opening 5 cm). Returns True if an object is held between them.

robot.release() -> None
    Open the fingers fully (5 cm gap).

robot.holding() -> name or None
robot.home() -> None              Move to a safe pose above the table.
robot.wait(seconds) -> None       Let time pass (max 5 s per call).
robot.log(*values) -> None        Write a debug note into the episode trace.

Safety layer (not negotiable): the tool point must stay inside x in [0.04, 0.32],
y in [-0.26, 0.26], z in [0.014, 0.26]. Targets up to 2 cm outside are clamped; further
out halts the skill. Pressing the gripper into the table with more than 30 N halts the
skill. Halts cannot be caught. Each episode has a time budget (simulated seconds).
Reachable band: roughly 0.10-0.23 m horizontal distance from the base at table height,
less when the tool point is high.

Good practice (any task)
- Perceive, act, verify, recover: re-read poses after important actions (for example check
  robot.holding() after robot.grasp()) and retry a bounded number of times if a check fails.
- Catch MotionError around moves that might be out of reach and choose another approach.
- Keep moves near objects slow (speed 0.05-0.10) and travel moves at the default speed.

Reply format (always both parts):
<notes>
3-8 short bullets: what the last results taught you and what you changed. Carry forward
useful facts from earlier notes.
</notes>
```python
# the complete skill module
```

reply:
<notes>
- First version: perceive both cubes by colour, average 3 noisy `get_pose` readings to fight the ~1 cm camera noise, then grasp the red cube with a small spiral of XY offsets so a bad reading doesn't doom the episode.
- Grasp at z=0.015 (cube centre height) with yaw = red cube's yaw so the fingers line up with its faces; verify with `robot.holding()` after every `grasp()`.
- After lifting, estimate the grasp offset (cube centre minus tool point) from a few fresh readings and subtract it when placing, so an off-centre grip doesn't shift the stack.
- Place by descending to z≈0.046 above the blue cube's averaged position (red bottom ≈ blue top at 0.030), release, retreat, then verify red is ~3 cm above blue and roughly aligned.
- All risky moves wrapped in try/except MotionError-style handling; slow speeds (0.05) near objects, default speed for travel.
- Bounded retries everywhere; return False on unrecoverable failure, True only after a successful stack check.
</notes>
```python
import math


def _avg_pos(robot, name, n=3):
    xs = []
    ys = []
    zs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        p = robot.get_pose(name)
        xs.append(p["pos"][0])
        ys.append(p["pos"][1])
        zs.append(p["pos"][2])
    return (sum(xs) / n, sum(ys) / n, sum(zs) / n)


def _find(robot, color):
    obs = robot.observe()
    for name, o in obs["objects"].items():
        if o.get("color") == color:
            return name
    return None


def run(robot):
    robot.home()

    red = _find(robot, "red")
    blue = _find(robot, "blue")
    if red is None or blue is None:
        robot.log("missing cubes", red, blue)
        return False

    red_yaw = robot.get_pose(red)["yaw"]

    # Spiral of small XY offsets to recover from a bad camera reading.
    offsets = [
        (0.0, 0.0),
        (0.006, 0.0), (-0.006, 0.0),
        (0.0, 0.006), (0.0, -0.006),
        (0.006, 0.006), (-0.006, -0.006),
        (0.006, -0.006), (-0.006, 0.006),
    ]

    grasped = False
    for dx, dy in offsets:
        x, y, z = _avg_pos(robot, red)
        tx, ty = x + dx, y + dy
        try:
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, yaw=red_yaw, speed=0.15)
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.015, yaw=red_yaw, speed=0.05)
        except Exception:
            try:
                robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, speed=0.15)
            except Exception:
                pass
            continue

        if robot.grasp() and robot.holding() == red:
            grasped = True
            break

        robot.release()
        try:
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, speed=0.15)
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not grasped:
        robot.log("failed to grasp red cube")
        return False

    # Lift straight up.
    try:
        robot.move_by(dz=0.08, speed=0.15)
    except Exception:
        pass

    if robot.holding() != red:
        robot.log("lost red cube during lift")
        return False

    # Estimate how far the cube centre sits from the tool point while held.
    off_x = 0.0
    off_y = 0.0
    try:
        n = 3
        gx = gy = rx = ry = 0.0
        for _ in range(n):
            g = robot.observe()["gripper"]["pos"]
            r = robot.get_pose(red)["pos"]
            gx += g[0]
            gy += g[1]
            rx += r[0]
            ry += r[1]
        ox = (rx - gx) / n
        oy = (ry - gy) / n
        # Only trust the estimate if it is small and plausible.
        if abs(ox) < 0.015 and abs(oy) < 0.015:
            off_x, off_y = ox, oy
    except Exception:
        pass

    bx, by, bz = _avg_pos(robot, blue)
    place_x = bx - off_x
    place_y = by - off_y
    place_z = 0.046  # red bottom ~0.031, blue top ~0.030

    try:
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, 0.12, speed=0.15)
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, place_z, speed=0.05)
    except Exception:
        robot.log("failed to reach place position")
        return False

    robot.release()
    try:
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, 0.12, speed=0.15)
    except Exception:
        pass
    robot.home()
    robot.wait(0.3)

    # Verify the stack.
    try:
        rp = robot.get_pose(red)["pos"]
        bp = robot.get_pose(blue)["pos"]
        dz = rp[2] - bp[2]
        dxy = math.hypot(rp[0] - bp[0], rp[1] - bp[1])
        robot.log("stack check dz=%.4f dxy=%.4f" % (dz, dxy))
        if dz > 0.02 and dxy < 0.025:
            return True
    except Exception:
        pass

    return False
```

def _avg_pos(robot, name, n=3):
    xs = []; ys = []; zs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        p = robot.get_pose(name)
        xs.append(p["pos"][0]); ys.append(p["pos"][1]); zs.append(p["pos"][2])
    return (sum(xs)/n, sum(ys)/n, sum(zs)/n)

def _find(robot, color):
    obs = robot.observe()
    for name, o in obs["objects"].items():
        if o.get("color") == color:
            return name
    return None

def run(robot):
    robot.home()
    red = _find(robot, "red")
    blue = _find(robot, "blue")
    if red is None or blue is None:
        robot.log("missing cubes", red, blue)
        return False

    red_yaw = robot.get_pose(red)["yaw"]

    offsets = [(0.0, 0.0), (0.006, 0.0), (-0.006, 0.0), (0.0, 0.006), (0.0, -0.006),
               (0.006, 0.006), (-0.006, -0.006), (0.006, -0.006), (-0.006, 0.006)]
    grasped = False
    for dx, dy in offsets:
        x, y, z = _avg_pos(robot, red)
        tx, ty = x + dx, y + dy
        try:
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, yaw=red_yaw, speed=0.15)
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.015, yaw=red_yaw, speed=0.05)
        except Exception:
            try:
                robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, speed=0.15)
            except Exception:
                pass
            continue
        if robot.grasp() and robot.holding() == red:
            grasped = True
            break
        robot.release()
        try:
            robot.move_to(tx, ty, 0.08, speed=0.15)
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not grasped:
        robot.log("failed to grasp red cube")
        return False

    try:
        robot.move_by(dz=0.08, speed=0.15)
    except Exception:
        pass

    # estimate grasp offset (cube centre relative to tool point)
    off_x = 0.0
    off_y = 0.0
    try:
        gx = 0.0; gy = 0.0; rx = 0.0; ry = 0.0
        n = 3
        for _ in range(n):
            g = robot.observe()["gripper"]["pos"]
            r = robot.get_pose(red)["pos"]
            gx += g[0]; gy += g[1]; rx += r[0]; ry += r[1]
        ox = (rx - gx) / n
        oy = (ry - gy) / n
        if abs(ox) < 0.02 and abs(oy) < 0.02:
            off_x, off_y = ox, oy
    except Exception:
        pass

    bx, by, bz = _avg_pos(robot, blue)
    place_x = bx - off_x
    place_y = by - off_y
    place_z = 0.046

    try:
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, 0.12, speed=0.15)
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, place_z, speed=0.05)
    except Exception:
        robot.log("failed to reach place position")
        return False

    robot.release()
    try:
        robot.move_to(place_x, place_y, 0.12, speed=0.15)
    except Exception:
        pass
    robot.home()
    robot.wait(0.3)

    try:
        rp = robot.get_pose(red)["pos"]
        bp = robot.get_pose(blue)["pos"]
        dz = rp[2] - bp[2]
        dxy = math.hypot(rp[0] - bp[0], rp[1] - bp[1])
        robot.log("stack check", dz, dxy)
        if dz > 0.02 and dxy < 0.025:
            return True
    except Exception:
        pass
    return False
